INtime Coder — how the form works and what you get

עברית

INtime, the mature real-time OS, now closes the loop with AI: describe your real-time application in a short form, and it comes back built, run on real INtime nodes, measured and filmed.

The form asks a few questions in your own words — the period, the I/O, the protocol and addresses — and reads them aloud if you want. Your e-mail address, written in the form, is where the result goes. The red button saves one file, <yourname>_filled_form.json.

When you fill in the details of your application, you choose one of three types of I/O:

  1. No I/O — all interactions are between objects of INtime.
  2. Ethernet — a TCP/IP interface to an I/O unit.
  3. The interfaces and protocols that UEI offers (https://www.ueidaq.com/).

Claude Code builds not only the code of your application but also the simulator (for types 2 and 3). The simulator is loaded into NodeB, so it is a real-time simulator, connected to your NodeA code over ven0 — exactly as a UEI box is connected to the host PC.

So please include in the form the behaviour you expect from the devices connected through these interfaces.

This is one of the most important things this way of evaluating allows. As NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said recently:

"How does an AI know that the actions that it's performing are consistent with what it should do if it doesn't have the ability to simulate the response of the physical world back on its actions? The response of its actions is really important to simulate. Otherwise, there's no way to evaluate it."

One ZIP: your solution for Visual Studio 2019 and 2022, and a narrated recording of the screens of the computer that ran it.

The result comes as an e-mail from our bench with two links: the recording (an .mp4 — plays on a phone or a PC) and the ZIP (for a Windows PC). If Drive asks you to request access, press it.

You need no Visual Studio, INtime or AI account — it all runs on our bench. Have INtime and Visual Studio? Build the solution, change it, run it. If not, watch the recording.
